title: B2B Product-Led Growth, Freemium vs. Free Trial, and Growth Loops
guest_role: Head of Growth, Dropbox & Amplitude; Interim CMO, Miro
description: Elena Verna shares actionable playbooks on B2B product-led growth (PLG), setting monetization paywalls, choosing between freemium vs free trials, and building compounding growth loops.
transcript_text:
Lenny: Elena Verna is back on the show. Elena, you have advised almost every major PLG unicorn—Miro, Amplitude, Dropbox, Netlify. When companies want to shift from sales-led to product-led growth, what is the biggest mistake they make?

Elena Verna: Hi Lenny! The biggest mistake is treating PLG as a top-of-funnel marketing strategy or just adding a self-serve checkout button. PLG is an organizational transformation where the product itself acts as the primary vehicle to acquire, activate, monetize, and retain users.

Lenny: How should founders decide between a Freemium model versus a 14-day Free Trial?

Elena Verna: Freemium is an acquisition and retention play. You use Freemium when your product has strong viral or collaborative loops, a huge addressable market, and when users need weeks or months to realize ongoing compounding value—like Miro or Notion. Free Trial, on the other hand, is a conversion acceleration play. You use Free Trials when your product provides fast, immediate value within hours, but costs real infrastructure to support and has a narrower target market.

Lenny: What is your framework for choosing which features to place behind the paid paywall?

Elena Verna: Never put your core 'aha' moment behind a paywall! You want users to experience value completely friction-free. Monetize on three vectors:
1. Usage and Volume: Number of boards, export resolution, API calls, storage.
2. Collaboration & Team features: Shared team workspaces, admin permissions, SSO, audit logs.
3. Advanced / Power workflows: Custom integrations, enterprise compliance, and advanced analytics.

Lenny: And how do growth loops replace traditional marketing funnels?

Elena Verna: Funnels are linear: you pour money in at the top, and a fraction drips out at the bottom. Once you stop paying for ads, growth stops. A Growth Loop is closed: the action of one cohort of users directly generates fuel to acquire the next cohort. In Miro, when a PM creates a whiteboard and invites 5 engineers to collaborate, those 5 engineers experience the product and create their own boards, inviting another 25 users. That is how Miro scaled to tens of millions of users without massive ad spend.
